title: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
provenance: community report with a full teardown (highball-db#6, Michael-Liendo), unverified by Highball
notes: Runs on Highball's native arm64 preview engine (arm64-wine11.18-r3, shown to installs with the preview key), through vkd3d-proton on MoltenVK; the game's recipe asks for that engine and sets the feature level, shader model and other variables it needs. Flies at 22 to 25 fps at the Medium preset with FSR Balanced in 1080p on a base M4 with 32 GB, with short GPU stalls now rare, a crash during the world load about one start in sixteen, seven minutes to the start screen and four more to the cockpit. On the Intel engines it does not launch: on the D3DMetal path the game refuses to start with 'Your graphics card does not support Shader Model 6.7'; D3DMetal reports Shader Model 6.6. A contributor confirmed the D3DMetal libraries Highball ships are byte-identical to CrossOver's, so no Wine frontend changes this - the ceiling is Apple's to lift. It is a gap rather than a hardware limit: Shader Model 6.7 only requires QuadAny/QuadAll and wave ops including helper lanes on top of 6.6, all of which Metal can already express, and the advanced texture operations are optional. Replacing the translation chain does not help either: stock vkd3d-proton cannot create a device on MoltenVK at all, failing earlier on missing transform feedback. Corrected from the original report: tiled resources tier 2 is NOT missing from Apple hardware. Metal supports sparse textures from the Apple6 GPU family and placement sparse buffers and textures on Apple8 and later, and D3DMetal itself calls those APIs; the gap is that MoltenVK implements no Vulkan sparse. Full teardown in the issue. The reporter's probes, DXVK patches and write-up are at github.com/Michael-Liendo/msfs2024-apple-silicon (probe.c measures the shader model directly, no game needed; the vkd3d-proton diffs themselves were lost, the README says what each did).
startNotice: The start screen comes about seven minutes after Play and the cockpit four minutes after Start. The loading screen shows the progress.

verified.fps: 22 to 25 parked, 17 to 20 on the take-off roll, Medium + FSR Balanced, 1080p
